hypothesis: If whorl breadths (equivalently conch diameters one revolution apart) expand by a factor r per whorl, the constant angle is alpha = arccot(ln r / 2 pi) (Thompson's own table: r = 1.5 -> 86.3 deg, 2.0 -> 83.7 deg, 2.5 -> 81.7 deg, 3.0 -> 80.1 deg, 3.5 -> 78.7 deg). The claim then predicts: Nautilus r about 3, alpha about 80 deg; for ordinary ammonoids and typically spiral gastropods alpha is usually between 80 and 85 deg (r between 1.72 and 3.00) and very seldom below 80 deg (r > 3.00).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. (a) Nautilus pompilius: per specimen, the median whorl expansion rate WER (Korn's definition, (dm1/dm2)^2 over half a whorl, which equals the per-revolution diameter ratio r) over all measured post-embryonic stages; the median across specimens, converted to alpha, must lie in [78, 82] deg (r in 2.6-3.5). (b) Ammonoids: per species, the median WER over measured stages with conch diameter >= 5 mm (excluding the embryonic ammonitella), converted to alpha; at least 50% of species must have alpha in [80, 85] deg and at most 10% alpha < 80 deg. (c) Gastropods: per specimen (then averaged per species), the fitted per-revolution whorl expansion rate W from the Collins et al. 2021 helicospiral fits, converted to alpha the same way; at least 50% of species in [80, 85] deg and at most 10% below 80 deg. All three of (a), (b), (c) must hold for 'supports'.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if the Nautilus median alpha is outside [76, 84] deg, or if in either the ammonoid or the gastropod sample fewer than 40% of species fall in [80, 85] deg, or more than 20% fall below 80 deg. Anything between the pass and fail thresholds is 'mixed'. If the gastropod expansion parameter cannot be mapped to a per-revolution ratio from the dataset's documentation, part (c) is reported as not operationalizable and the verdict rests on (a) and (b) with a caveat.
interpretation: Thompson defines the constant angle through the per-whorl ratio of radii or whorl breadths, r = e^(2 pi cot alpha), and reads the angle off that ratio; the test therefore measures r and converts it with his own formula rather than fitting tangent angles to outlines. Modern 'whorl expansion rate' (Korn: WER = (dm1/dm2)^2 across half a whorl; Raup: W per revolution) is the same quantity for a planispiral shell. 'Ordinary ammonitoid shells' is operationalized as the species in a large published cross-section dataset (Devonian-Jurassic), 'typically spiral gastropods' as the 25 fossil and modern helicospiral species measured by Collins et al. 2021; neither sample was chosen by the tester.
